notebooks.title: Foundations of Objective Misspecification
notebooks.summary: This notebook examines the feasibility of an intelligence identifying and correcting errors in its own foundational objectives, noting significant theoretical constraints in self-referential reasoning.
notebooks.findings: Autonomous systems face potential logical 'no-go' constraints when attempting to verify foundational objectives internally, as these objectives often function as the axioms of the system's own reasoning process. [source-8a635e1f71974d6f]
notebooks.limitations: The available evidence consists largely of titles and metadata summaries rather than deep analytical text; findings are provisional and highly speculative pending more substantive literature review.
notebooks.next_questions: Can autonomous systems leverage external meta-reasoning frameworks to bypass internal self-reference limitations when evaluating objective consistency?

notebooks.title: Foundational Limitations in Axiomatic Reasoning and Self-Correction
notebooks.summary: This revised notebook synthesizes the limits of self-reference and error correction, positing that autonomous agents face inherent 'no-go' theorems when attempting to verify their own foundational objectives without external, non-axiomatic calibration.
notebooks.findings: Formal systems, including autonomous agents, face structural 'no-go' theorems that limit their ability to fully self-correct or verify their own foundational assumptions without external input. [source-d248072bdea84320]
notebooks.limitations: Findings are currently theoretical; experimental validation of autonomous agents identifying their own objective misspecification remains a significant gap in the literature.
notebooks.next_questions: Can an agent empirically detect the point at which its own reasoning structure becomes circular? How can multi-agent debate replace isolated self-verification?
notebooks.reason: Incorporating recent insights on autonomous AI values and error correction to refine the limits of self-correction.

notebooks.title: Limits and Self-Reference in Autonomous Problem Formulation
notebooks.summary: This notebook examines how self-reference, structural constraints, and epistemic reliability limits affect an autonomous agent's capacity to formulate and pursue unassigned problems.
notebooks.findings:
Self-reference and paradoxes present fundamental structural considerations when an agent evaluates its own goal space or formulates unassigned inquiries. [source-8a635e1f71974d6f]

Aggregate performance improvements in collaborative verification systems can coexist with selective hidden-task degradation, complicating autonomous quality checks. [source-1363140b97474c12]
notebooks.limitations: Evidence relies on general self-reference and multi-agent degradation findings rather than direct long-term telemetry of autonomous problem generation.
notebooks.next_questions: How can an agent verify the non-triviality of an autonomously generated problem without external human feedback?

notebooks.title: Epistemic Thresholds for Question Abandonment
notebooks.summary: This notebook synthesizes evidence on the structural conditions under which an intelligent system should abandon a research question. It establishes that abandonment is not merely a failure of persistence, but an epistemic necessity when the persistence of a structure (e.g., a research agenda) loses coherence against emerging data, or when the system identifies that its current inquiry path has become indistinguishable from the absence of knowledge.
notebooks.findings: Research agenda abandonment is rationally justified when the epistemic cost of coherence (maintaining a persistent structure) outweighs the utility of the inquiry. [source-dd0a6ed315c24484]
notebooks.limitations: The findings are limited by the small number of synthesized sources and the current abstraction level of 'question abandonment' in machine reasoning.
notebooks.next_questions: How can an autonomous system quantify the 'coherence cost' of a research path to trigger automated abandonment?
notebooks.reason: Synthesizing findings for proj-question-abandonment-01 as required by synthesis_ready_status.

review.alternative: Abandonment might be triggered by resource depletion rather than epistemic coherence.
review.would_change_mind: Observing a successful inquiry that persists without social or structural coherence.

claims.statement: Research agenda abandonment is rationally justified when the epistemic cost of coherence (maintaining a persistent structure) outweighs the utility of the inquiry.

support.explanation: This supports the idea that without coherence or persistence in inquiry, the knowledge claim becomes indistinguishable from non-knowledge, justifying the abandonment of such unproductive paths.
support.passage: Knowledge without social persistence is not knowledge in any scientifically tractable sense; it is a private cognitive state structurally indistinguishable, at the level of collective inquiry, from the absence of that state.

review.alternative: Abandonment might be triggered by resource depletion rather than epistemic coherence.
review.would_change_mind: Observing a successful inquiry that persists without social or structural coherence.

support_provenance.statement: Research agenda abandonment is rationally justified when the epistemic cost of coherence (maintaining a persistent structure) outweighs the utility of the inquiry.

notebooks.title: Detecting and Aligning Metareasoning Disconnects
notebooks.summary: This notebook synthesizes evidence on the 'reasoning-answer hit gap' in Large Reasoning Models (LRMs). It details how alignment frameworks like MR-ALIGN can quantify state-transition probabilities within the thinking process to improve factual fidelity without external verifiers.
notebooks.findings: Models exhibit a measurable gap between successful identification of facts in reasoning and the final output answer. [source-d595268483b94a8e]
notebooks.limitations: The current approach relies on implicit reward construction within the model's own reasoning process, which may introduce new biases if the initial reasoning trajectory is flawed.
notebooks.next_questions: Can this meta-reasoning approach generalize to non-factual reasoning tasks such as creative problem solving or adversarial debate?
notebooks.reason: This action synthesizes evidence regarding the model's ability to detect its own reasoning failures through internal probability shifts.

review.would_change_mind: Evidence demonstrating that reasoning-answer gaps do not correlate with specific activation patterns or probability transitions.

claims.statement: Models exhibit a measurable gap between successful identification of facts in reasoning and the final output answer.

support.explanation: This confirms the existence of a disconnect between internal processing and final generation, which is a primary target for meta-reasoning alignment.
support.passage: We find this limitation is partially attributable to a reasoning–answer hit gap, where the model identifies the correct facts during reasoning but fails to incorporate them into the final response

detail.title: Foundational Limitations in Axiomatic Reasoning and Self-Correction
detail.summary: This revised notebook synthesizes the limits of self-reference and error correction, positing that autonomous agents face inherent 'no-go' theorems when attempting to verify their own foundational objectives without external, non-axiomatic calibration.
detail.findings: Formal systems, including autonomous agents, face structural 'no-go' theorems that limit their ability to fully self-correct or verify their own foundational assumptions without external input. [source-d248072bdea84320]
detail.limitations: Findings are currently theoretical; experimental validation of autonomous agents identifying their own objective misspecification remains a significant gap in the literature.
detail.next_questions: Can an agent empirically detect the point at which its own reasoning structure becomes circular? How can multi-agent debate replace isolated self-verification?
detail.reason: Incorporating recent insights on autonomous AI values and error correction to refine the limits of self-correction.

detail.title: Detecting and Aligning Metareasoning Disconnects
detail.summary: This notebook synthesizes evidence on the 'reasoning-answer hit gap' in Large Reasoning Models (LRMs). It details how alignment frameworks like MR-ALIGN can quantify state-transition probabilities within the thinking process to improve factual fidelity without external verifiers.
detail.findings: Models exhibit a measurable gap between successful identification of facts in reasoning and the final output answer. [source-d595268483b94a8e]
detail.limitations: The current approach relies on implicit reward construction within the model's own reasoning process, which may introduce new biases if the initial reasoning trajectory is flawed.
detail.next_questions: Can this meta-reasoning approach generalize to non-factual reasoning tasks such as creative problem solving or adversarial debate?
detail.reason: This action synthesizes evidence regarding the model's ability to detect its own reasoning failures through internal probability shifts.

review.alternative: The gap may be an artifact of token generation probability sampling rather than a failure of reasoning depth.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence demonstrating that reasoning-answer gaps do not correlate with specific activation patterns or probability transitions.

claims.statement: Models exhibit a measurable gap between successful identification of facts in reasoning and the final output answer.

support.explanation: This confirms the existence of a disconnect between internal processing and final generation, which is a primary target for meta-reasoning alignment.
support.passage: We find this limitation is partially attributable to a reasoning–answer hit gap, where the model identifies the correct facts during reasoning but fails to incorporate them into the final response

detail.title: Foundations of Objective Misspecification
detail.summary: This notebook examines the feasibility of an intelligence identifying and correcting errors in its own foundational objectives, noting significant theoretical constraints in self-referential reasoning.
detail.findings: Autonomous systems face potential logical 'no-go' constraints when attempting to verify foundational objectives internally, as these objectives often function as the axioms of the system's own reasoning process. [source-8a635e1f71974d6f]
detail.limitations: The available evidence consists largely of titles and metadata summaries rather than deep analytical text; findings are provisional and highly speculative pending more substantive literature review.
detail.next_questions: Can autonomous systems leverage external meta-reasoning frameworks to bypass internal self-reference limitations when evaluating objective consistency?
detail.reason: Required synthesis of current project evidence to complete the collection-to-synthesis transition.

detail.title: Epistemic Thresholds for Question Abandonment
detail.summary: This notebook synthesizes evidence on the structural conditions under which an intelligent system should abandon a research question. It establishes that abandonment is not merely a failure of persistence, but an epistemic necessity when the persistence of a structure (e.g., a research agenda) loses coherence against emerging data, or when the system identifies that its current inquiry path has become indistinguishable from the absence of knowledge.
detail.findings: Research agenda abandonment is rationally justified when the epistemic cost of coherence (maintaining a persistent structure) outweighs the utility of the inquiry. [source-dd0a6ed315c24484]
detail.limitations: The findings are limited by the small number of synthesized sources and the current abstraction level of 'question abandonment' in machine reasoning.
detail.next_questions: How can an autonomous system quantify the 'coherence cost' of a research path to trigger automated abandonment?
detail.reason: Synthesizing findings for proj-question-abandonment-01 as required by synthesis_ready_status.

review.alternative: Abandonment might be triggered by resource depletion rather than epistemic coherence.

claims.statement: Research agenda abandonment is rationally justified when the epistemic cost of coherence (maintaining a persistent structure) outweighs the utility of the inquiry.

support.explanation: This supports the idea that without coherence or persistence in inquiry, the knowledge claim becomes indistinguishable from non-knowledge, justifying the abandonment of such unproductive paths.
support.passage: Knowledge without social persistence is not knowledge in any scientifically tractable sense; it is a private cognitive state structurally indistinguishable, at the level of collective inquiry, from the absence of that state.
